skill.name: mantis-patch
skill.description: Generate minimal fixes for reproduced security findings, verify them against baseline tests, and record patch diffs. Restore source changes after testing.
skill.summary: Guide security patching with snapshot checks, transactional rollback, benign controls, and independent attack testing.
skill.author: google

security_audit.summary: All 250 static alerts are false positives: their context shows Markdown formatting, workflow metadata, temporary copies, and verification checks rather than the reported threats. Two semantic risks remain: stored reproducer commands lack required host confinement, and helper reuse relies on a forgeable version comment. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection, credential collection, or deliberate data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Stored reproducer commands execute without a mandatory host security boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Require reviewed commands in restricted containers with no host secrets, network disabled by default, and only necessary writable mounts.

remediation.issue: A helper version comment does not authenticate executable content.
remediation.suggestion: Regenerate helpers from trusted templates or verify complete content and provenance before execution. Reject symlinks and prevent replacement between verification and execution.

semantic_findings.title: Stored Commands Lack Mandatory Host Isolation
semantic_findings.description: The skill executes run_command from finding records after path substitution. Mandatory shadow copies protect source changes but do not confine process permissions or network access. If commands or reproducers are compromised, they can access host resources unless the caller supplies an additional sandbox.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Stored-command execution is explicit, while containers and namespaces are optional alternatives to source copies. Host confinement is not required; exploitation depends on compromised inputs.

semantic_findings.title: Version Marker Used To Trust Executable Helpers
semantic_findings.description: Helper reuse checks its first line for MANTIS_HELPER_VERSION = 2, then instructs execution of the existing script. An attacker with helper write access can preserve that comment while replacing executable content. The version check does not establish helper integrity or provenance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly permit execution after a first-line marker check. The integrity gap is clear; exploitation requires control over the helper file.

content.user_title: Generate and Verify Minimal Security Patches
content.value_statement: Security fixes can fail when verification uses stale code or broken test harnesses. This skill guides minimal patches with snapshot checks, baseline tests, and independent re-attacks.
actual_capabilities: Guide minimal source fixes for reproduced findings, using mandatory temporary shadows when snapshots are pinned.
Check snapshot provenance and reopen findings whose earlier verification belongs to a different snapshot.
Require unpatched baseline evidence, a successful patched build, and a benign control before verified status.
Coordinate an independent re-attack with at least three valid input variants before verified status.
Record unified patch diffs, finding histories, and learning entries, then restore modified source or remove temporary shadows.
Rebase eligible archived patches and propose mitigation guidance for binary-only targets.
limitations: Provides workflow instructions, not a standalone patching engine; it requires existing Mantis findings and does not perform initial vulnerability discovery.
Independent re-attacks require a separate mantis-reproduce subagent that is not included in this skill.
Binary-only targets receive mitigation recommendations, not binary patches.
Source shadow copies do not enforce host security isolation, and helper version markers do not authenticate executable content.

use_cases.title: Remediate Reproduced Vulnerabilities
use_cases.description: Create a minimal source fix and collect baseline, benign-control, and re-attack results for an existing reproduced finding.

use_cases.title: Review Fixes After Source Changes
use_cases.description: Reopen stale findings and rebase eligible archived patches onto a new snapshot before verification.

use_cases.title: Assess Binary-Only Mitigations
use_cases.description: Produce mitigation recommendations for firmware or compiled targets when source code is unavailable.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Ready Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mantis-patch to identify eligible findings in [state_root]. Summarize required inputs and blockers without running commands or editing source.

prompt_templates.title: Patch One Reproduced Finding
prompt_templates.prompt: Patch finding [finding_id] using snapshot [snapshot_root] and state directory [state_root]. Review commands, verify helper integrity, and require a restricted execution environment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: generate a minimal fix for one known issue.

prompt_templates.title: Verify A Patch Thoroughly
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify finding [finding_id] inside a restricted execution environment. Require baseline evidence, matching sanitizer flags, benign controls, and independent re-attacks; report missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate correctness and prevent unsupported success claims.

prompt_templates.title: Rebase Archived Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review stale findings against [snapshot_root] and verify helper integrity. Rebase only eligible fixes, test in restricted environments, extract diffs, and roll back changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: reuse prior fixes after snapshot changes.

output: Illustrative result: Patch verification passed for the current snapshot and tested vulnerability.
The unpatched baseline triggered the issue; the patched build compiled and the benign control reached the target without crashing.

output_examples.input: Assess a reproduced firmware issue without source code.
output: Restrict access to the affected interface and pursue a vendor-supported firmware correction.
The finding record contains mitigation guidance rather than a source diff.

output: Initial verification passed, but the independent re-attack did not complete.
No verified-secure claim was recorded; the finding remains eligible for further verification.

best_practices: Review finding records and reproducer commands before execution in a restricted environment without host secrets.
Use pinned snapshots and private shadow copies to keep baseline code unchanged.
Verify complete helper content and require baseline evidence, benign controls, consistent sanitizers, and independent re-attacks.
anti_patterns: Run unreviewed commands from finding records directly on a sensitive host.
Trust an existing helper solely because its first line contains the expected version marker.
Claim verified security after missing files, failed builds, stale baselines, or incomplete re-attacks.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Mantis finding records, target source or binary artifacts, and reproducer details for runnable verification.

faq.question: Does it discover new vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It targets reproduced findings and exploit-chain records rather than initial vulnerability research.

faq.question: Does it leave fixes applied to the source tree?
faq.answer: No. It extracts patch diffs and restores the original source or removes temporary shadows after processing.

faq.question: What happens when source code is unavailable?
faq.answer: It proposes mitigation guidance and does not attempt binary modification.

faq.question: What is required for verified-secure status?
faq.answer: Baseline evidence, successful compilation, benign controls, consistent sanitizer settings, and independent re-attacks are required. This status does not guarantee absence of other vulnerabilities.

faq.question: Are temporary shadow directories a security sandbox?
faq.answer: No. They isolate source changes, not host access. Use restricted execution and review stored commands and helpers.
